text:
Pavel Dorofeyev scored 37 goals for Vegas last season, and his start in New York has been a test of patience. The chances have come: his shots add up to 7.5 expected goals (the quality of his looks), and only five have gone in. The bigger number is the luck around him. With Dorofeyev on the ice, the Rangers have scored 15.9 fewer goals than their chances deserved, a gap so large it almost has to close.

That's why we aren't worried. His five-on-five numbers are good: the Rangers get 55% of the expected goals with him on, four points better than without him. His power-play goal in the win over Philadelphia on Nov. 5 made The New York Times' takeaways ("Pavel Dorofeyev breaks through"), and the New York Post called it his first big Rangers moment. The Hockey News says the Rangers are still searching for the best version of him. Our numbers say that version is already here; the goals are just running late.
headline: The goals are running late
